Hi Meera — thanks for the sample.

Short answer: yes, we can support a split/pro-rata approach, but we need two things to be clean: (A) per-line supply classification (service vs. subscription) on the invoice, and (B) validated VAT/GST IDs for the recipient legal entities. Our usual flow is to reissue a split invoice (separate line items + tax flags) once VATID validation passes. We can also provide a self-bill style CSV export that your AP team can ingest.

Quick clarifying questions to speed this:
- Are the GSTIDs in your CSV already validated by TransGlobal accounting, or do you want Redwood to attempt validation? (our validation tooling checks registry + format + active status where available)
- For mixed supply, do you want separate invoices per legal entity, or a single invoice with split lines flagged for reverse-charge?

I'll loop in Karthik (billing ops) for the reissue workflow and Jordan (account exec) for the approval/contract side if a formal credit/reissue is needed. If you can confirm validation preference we can aim to deliver a patched invoice + a self-bill CSV within 48 hours.

Ben / Jordan — operational note on options we can offer: 

Option A (recommended): reissue a single invoice that includes per-line tax treatment flags + tax_id_reference column. This preserves one document for AP reconciliation while making reverse-charge obvious for services lines. We'll attach a machine-readable CSV (self-bill export) with one row per invoiceline: invoice_id, legal_entity, line_type (service|subscription), taxable_flag, tax_rate, tax_amount, customer_tax_id, validation_status.

Option B: split into two invoices per legal entity (one for subscription access, one for services). Cleaner for jurisdictions that treat platform access differently, but increases invoice volume and may complicate your GL mapping.

Validation approach: Redwood can run a two-pass check: format/regex check (instant) + registry lookup (where public registries exist) that returns HIGH/LOW confidence. We set HIGH confidence as a precondition for RC flagging. For AU and SG we have registry endpoints; HK is trickier (no central public GST register). For HK entities, we'd need documented evidence (tax registration letter) rather than registry verification.

If TransGlobal wants Redwood to attempt validation, we need the raw tax id column and legal_entity mapping in the CSV, and accept a small fee for manual follow-up on low-confidence items.

I can prepare a sample reissue payload and the self-bill CSV schema this afternoon.

— Karthik
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: APAC GST: proposed pro-rata split and VATID validation workflow

Hi Meera — following up with a proposed, minimal-impact workflow so your AP team can hit Friday's cut: 

1) Redwood runs an automated validation on the tax_id column in your CSV. Items that return HIGH confidence will be flagged RC-eligible for services lines. For LOW confidence (HK or ambiguous), we'll return a short evidence checklist and request a supporting document.

2) Once validation is complete we will: (a) reissue the quarterly invoice as a single PDF with per-line tax flags and (b) provide a self-bill CSV export mapping each invoice line to a legal_entity and tax treatment code. The PDF will include a brief note: "Lines flagged RC: reverse-charge applies where recipient provided valid tax id; see CSV for machine mapping."

3) If you prefer, we can instead issue two invoices per legal entity (subscription vs services). That requires accounting sign-off and may delay processing — we recommend the single invoice + machine mapping approach for speed.

Next steps I propose: you confirm whether Redwood should attempt validation (we can auto-validate AU/SG; HK will likely need evidence). If yes, please confirm CSV with a column named customer_tax_id and legal_entity_id and re-attach.

Deliverables and timing: validation run + provisional flags in 24 hours; reissued invoice + self-bill CSV in 48 hours after validation acceptance. If there are low-confidence items requiring manual evidence, we'll flag them immediately and pause reissue for those rows only.

I've attached a short PDF that shows the CSV schema and an example of the reissued invoice layout.

Thanks — Jordan will support account-side approvals if you need a credit note/offseting entry.

Best regards,
